storyline.resolution: until Fiji appoints a permanent head coach to lead them toward the 2027 Rugby World Cup

teams.heading: Fiji Sun says Warren Gatland is leading candidate, with players informed
teams.body: Fiji Sun reports that Warren Gatland, former Wales and British & Irish Lions coach, has emerged as the leading candidate for the Flying Fijians job, with players understood to have been told of his impending appointment. The union is reportedly finalising negotiations with its preferred candidate and could announce within 24 hours. Jake White, former Springboks coach, remains in contention, but his financial demands could be a stumbling block for the cash-strapped union, according to the same report.

lead.why: It is the only new development in today's coverage, moving the head coach race from Jake White to Warren Gatland.

teams.heading: England captain accuses 'far right' of using St George's flags to divide
teams.body: England's captain has accused the 'far right' of putting up St George's flags to 'divide' people, a claim reported in today's coverage. The remark places the team's captain in the middle of a debate over national symbols that goes well beyond the pitch. No further detail of the context or the captain's full comments has been reported today, and no response from the RFU or the dressing room has been carried in the coverage.

lead.why: It is the only genuinely new item in the shortlist, and an England captain taking on the 'far right' over St George's flags is a story fans will talk about beyond the rugby.

teams.heading: Robert Kitson's Guardian top six opens with France's 1977 grand slam side
teams.body: Robert Kitson's Guardian feature on the most inspiring teams in rugby history, published on 6 October, puts France first in his proposed top six: the side that won the 1977 Five Nations grand slam. Kitson says that French team sheet sent a shiver down the spine before a ball was kicked, and he frames the list around sides that still capture the imagination decades later rather than pure results.

lead.why: The only shortlist item that is France-centred and not already reported, though it is a background feature rather than fresh news.

teams.heading: Ireland women's Aoife Wafer ruled out of Japan and South Africa fixtures
teams.body: Ireland women's Aoife Wafer has been ruled out of Ireland's Japan game and South Africa Tests, with the injury first reported in late September. No return date has been reported since, and the coverage in today's press does not show her back in training or named in a squad. Until she is cleared, the absence remains open.

teams.heading: Scotland's last meeting with New Zealand ended in a 25-17 home defeat
teams.body: Scotland's next match is Round 4 against New Zealand, and the last meeting between the sides was a 25-17 home defeat in November 2025, played as an International Friendly. That is a single result, not a head-to-head record. In the log's three played matches, Scotland have won two and lost one, scoring 108 points and conceding 97, for a points difference of +11. The most recent result was a 33-17 win over Fiji in Round 3.

teams.heading: Jac Morgan hailed as superhuman as Wales hopeful admits confidence dip
teams.body: Jac Morgan is now being described as superhuman, and a Wales squad hopeful has admitted a dip in confidence, with Steve Tandy due to name his Nations Championship squad on 20 October. Morgan's form at Gloucester backs up the praise. He has been hugely impressive in all aspects since arriving, and his epic carry, bumping off four Leicester defenders, set up Will Trenholm's second-half try in Gloucester's 38-31 defeat at Welford Road last Friday.

lead.why: The only NEW item in the shortlist, and it is a different story from the Basham, WRU and Reffell pieces already run.

teams.heading: Mario Ledesma rejoins Pumas as forwards coach until 2027 World Cup
teams.body: The Argentine Rugby Union has confirmed Mario Ledesma, who won 84 Tests as a hooker and coached Argentina from 2018 to 2022, returns as forwards coach until the end of the 2027 World Cup. Ledesma said: "I am honoured and very grateful for the opportunity to work with Los Pumas again." He joins Shaun Edwards, the defence specialist, who arrives at the end of October once his Red Roses WXV commitments finish.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item with a new development in the pack (Ledesma's forwards role), separate from the Edwards timing already covered.

teams.heading: Steve Hansen questions Ben Donaldson's Test No.10 credentials after Eden Park thrashing
teams.body: Steve Hansen, former All Blacks head coach, has questioned whether Ben Donaldson is a good enough Test-level No.10, in the latest Rugby Unity episode. Speaking about last Saturday's 50-19 loss in Auckland, Hansen said the All Blacks had prepared for the high-ball contest Australia targeted, and that the Wallabies' tactic "bounced back at them" straight away. The Bledisloe Cup decider is in Sydney next Saturday.

lead.why: It is a fresh, named Australia story about the Wallabies' No.10 ahead of the Sydney decider, and it has not been covered in the earlier editions.

teams.heading: Ben Mowen's Stockman Rugby side tours Japan, opening in Kyoto against Doshisha
teams.body: Stockman Rugby have confirmed the players and staff for their Dark Horse tour of Japan, which opens on Wednesday 14 October against Doshisha University in Kyoto. Head coach Ben Mowen, a former assistant with Japan's women's team, said "I have a deep affection for the culture and people of Japan". The club hosted the Japan U23s earlier this year, and the Queensland Reds have also announced a late-2026 tour, as have NSW Junior Rugby Union's U15 boys and U16 girls development XVs.

lead.why: It is the freshest genuinely new item in the pack, and it is the only one that is about Japan's rugby future rather than a result or a story already run.

teams.heading: Jordie Barrett praised by former Wallaby Nick Phipps after Eden Park rout
teams.body: Former Wallabies scrum-half Nick Phipps says Jordie Barrett is in world-class form and that play is increasingly directed through him. Speaking on Between Two Posts, Phipps pointed to Barrett's catch of a box kick that set up an opening try in last Saturday's 50-19 win at Eden Park, and questioned how Wallaby Joseph Suaalii was positioned to receive it.

lead.why: It is a fresh, praise-led angle on Jordie Barrett from outside the New Zealand camp, and it is not the Barrett omission story already run today.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson says Wallabies had 'false sense of security' against rotated Boks
teams.body: Former New Zealand wing Jeff Wilson believes the Wallabies were given a misleading picture by their 42-38 win in Perth, where Springbok boss Rassie Erasmus had made 13 changes to his starting XV. Speaking on Sky Sport's The Breakdown, Wilson said the All Blacks came into their 50-19 win in Auckland better prepared, having faced the full-strength Boks in Rugby's Greatest Rivalry. He argued Australia had taken the wrong lesson from a rotated Springbok side.

lead.why: It is the most shareable Springbok storyline in today's pack, a former New Zealand wing judging the Boks' rotated Perth side and the Wallabies' response to it.
